title.source: Section check: Objects, making and power
title.back: Section check: Objects, making and power

intro.source: 10 questions about Lessons 1–5. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 10 questions about Lessons 1–5. No need to hurry. You can go back to the lessons and try again as many times as you like.

questions.0.question.source: Hokusai's wave print has many impressions. What is an impression?
questions.0.question.back: Hokusai's wave print has many impressions. What is an impression?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: A painting made for one room
questions.0.options.0.text.back: A painting made for one room

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A painting for one room is like The Harvesters. An impression is one printed copy. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A painting for one room is like The Harvesters. An impression is one printed copy. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: One printed copy from the blocks
questions.0.options.1.text.back: One copy printed from the blocks

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Many copies can be printed from the same wood blocks. Each copy is an impression.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The same set of wood blocks can print many copies. Each copy is one impression.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: The block of wood with the design
questions.0.options.2.text.back: The wooden block with the design on it

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The block holds the design. An impression is a copy printed on paper from it. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The block holds the design, while an impression is a copy printed from it onto paper. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.1.question.source: The Harvesters shows farm workers in 1565. Why can it not show the life of every farm worker?
questions.1.question.back: The Harvesters shows farm workers in 1565. Why can this picture not show the life of every farm worker?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: It shows its rich patron's view.
questions.1.options.0.text.back: It shows the view of its rich patron

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A rich merchant in Antwerp ordered it for his house. The museum says the scene is nicer than real life.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. A rich merchant in Antwerp ordered this picture for his house. The museum says the picture looks nicer than real life.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: It was painted by the farm workers.
questions.1.options.1.text.back: The farm workers painted it themselves

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Bruegel painted it for a rich merchant in the city. The workers did not choose how they were shown. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Bruegel painted this picture for a rich merchant in the city. The workers did not choose how they would be painted. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: It is a print made for many buyers.
questions.1.options.2.text.back: It is a print made for many buyers

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The Harvesters is an oil painting on wood. It was made for one patron and one room. Look back at Lesson 1.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The Harvesters is an oil painting on wood. It was made for one patron and one room. Go back to Lesson 1.

questions.2.question.source: In batik, melted wax is a resist. What does a resist do?
questions.2.question.back: In batik, melted wax is a resist. What does a resist do?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: It makes all the colours much brighter.
questions.2.options.0.text.back: It makes all the colours on the cloth much brighter

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The dye gives the colour. The wax keeps the dye off some parts. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The dye gives the colour, while the wax keeps the dye off some parts. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: It adds gold leaf to the whole cloth.
questions.2.options.1.text.back: It puts gold leaf over the whole cloth

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Gold leaf is called prada. A resist keeps the dye off parts of the cloth. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Gold leaf is called prada. A resist keeps the dye off parts of the cloth. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: It keeps dye off part of the cloth.
questions.2.options.2.text.back: It keeps dye off part of the cloth

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The wax protects the parts the maker chooses. Then the dye colours the rest.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. The wax protects the parts the maker chose, then the dye colours the rest.

questions.3.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A museum shows a batik skirt from a town on the north coast of Java. It was made in the 1800s. Its label says: "This skirt shows what all Javanese people wore at that time."
questions.3.stimulus.body.note: "the 1800s" is written with the years (ช่วงปี 1800 ถึง 1899), as in the lessons.
questions.3.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A museum displays a batik skirt from a town on the north coast of Java. This cloth was made between 1800 and 1899. Its label says: "This skirt shows how all Javanese people dressed at that time."

questions.3.question.source: Which change would make this label more accurate?
questions.3.question.back: Which change would make this label more accurate?

questions.3.options.0.text.source: Say it shows what all of Indonesia wore
questions.3.options.0.text.back: Say it shows how all of Indonesia dressed

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. That makes the claim even bigger. One cloth cannot show what everyone wore. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. That makes the claim even bigger. One cloth cannot show how everyone dressed. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: Say it shows one place's tradition
questions.3.options.1.text.back: Say it shows one place's tradition

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. A cloth shows one place and its makers. It does not show what every Javanese person wore.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. A cloth shows one place and its makers there. It does not show how every Javanese person dressed.

questions.3.options.2.text.source: Take away the place where it was made
questions.3.options.2.text.back: Remove the place where it was made

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The place helps explain the cloth. Places in Java had different traditions. Look back at Lesson 2.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The place helps explain this cloth. Different places in Java had different traditions. Go back to Lesson 2.

questions.4.question.source: Why are ceramics useful evidence of links between places?
questions.4.question.back: Why are ceramics useful evidence of links between places?

questions.4.options.0.text.source: Fired clay lasts, and many were made.
questions.4.options.0.text.back: Fired clay lasts, and many were made

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Fired clay survives well. People made very many pots, so lots of them are left to study.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. Fired clay survives well. People made a great many pots, so many are left to study.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: They were made only for rulers at court.
questions.4.options.1.text.back: They were made only for rulers at court

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Makers made everyday pots for many buyers, at home and far away. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Makers produced everyday pots for many buyers, both at home and far away. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: Each one tells us who bought it and where.
questions.4.options.2.text.back: Each one tells who bought it and where

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The dish from the shipwreck does not tell us who bought it. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The dish from the shipwreck does not tell us who bought it. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.5.question.source: A bronze box made in China has Arabic writing on its lid. What can the box show us?
questions.5.question.back: A bronze box made in China has Arabic writing on its lid. What can this box show us?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Who used the box in their home each day
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Who used this box at home every day

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The box does not tell us who used it. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The box does not tell us who used it. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: That the box was sent to another country
questions.5.options.1.text.back: That the box was sent to another country

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The writing does not prove the box went abroad. Look back at Lesson 3.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The writing does not prove the box went abroad. Go back to Lesson 3.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: One object can link two traditions
questions.5.options.2.text.back: One object can link two traditions

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. It joins Chinese making with Arabic religious words. One place name cannot tell its whole story.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. This box joins Chinese making with religious words in Arabic. A single place name cannot tell its whole story.

questions.6.question.source: The false beard on the sphinx was a convention. What is a convention?
questions.6.question.back: The false beard on the sphinx was a convention. What is a convention?

questions.6.options.0.text.source: A gift that people gave to a god
questions.6.options.0.text.back: A gift that people offered to a god

questions.6.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Offerings were gifts. A convention is a usual way of showing something, like a king's false beard. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.6.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Offerings were gifts. A convention is the usual way of showing something, like a king's false beard. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.6.options.1.text.source: A new idea that no one used before
questions.6.options.1.text.back: A new idea that no one had used before

questions.6.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A convention is the opposite. It is a usual way that many people used. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.6.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A convention is the opposite. It is a usual way that many people used. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.6.options.2.text.source: A usual way of showing something
questions.6.options.2.text.back: A usual way of showing something

questions.6.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. Egyptian kings were usually shown with a false beard. Hatshepsut's images followed this way.
questions.6.options.2.feedback.back: Correct. Egyptian kings were usually shown with a false beard. Hatshepsut's images followed this way.

questions.7.question.source: How did the Moche ear ornament show that a person had high status?
questions.7.question.back: How did the Moche ear ornament show that a person had high status?

questions.7.options.0.text.source: Costly materials, skill, and wearing it
questions.7.options.0.text.back: Costly materials, skill, and wearing it

questions.7.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Gold, stones and shell, joined with skill, showed a person's rank on their body.
questions.7.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. Gold, stones and shell, joined with skill, showed that person's rank on their body.

questions.7.options.1.text.source: Its huge size, inside a temple building
questions.7.options.1.text.back: Its huge size, standing in a temple

questions.7.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. That is the sphinx. The ornament was small, and people wore it on the body. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.7.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. That is the sphinx. The ear ornament was small, and people wore it on the body. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.7.options.2.text.source: Writing on it that gives the owner's name
questions.7.options.2.text.back: Writing on it that gives the owner's name

questions.7.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. The ornament shows a runner with wings. Its gold, stones and shell showed rank. Look back at Lesson 4.
questions.7.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. The ear ornament shows a runner with wings. Its gold, stones and shell showed rank. Go back to Lesson 4.

questions.8.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. Queen Tamsa collects fine pages. One page has writing made 100 years before her time. Her painters add new flower borders around it. Then the page goes into her album, next to new paintings.
questions.8.stimulus.body.note: The made-up queen is referred to with พระนาง, as Hatshepsut is in Lesson 4.
questions.8.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. Queen Tamsa collects beautiful pages. One page has writing made 100 years before her time. Her painters add new flower borders around that page. Then the page goes into her album, next to new paintings.

questions.8.question.source: Which idea from Lesson 5 does this example show?
questions.8.question.back: Which idea from Lesson 5 does this example show?

questions.8.options.0.text.source: Only new pictures can go in an album.
questions.8.options.0.text.back: Only new pictures can go in an album

questions.8.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The Shah Jahan Album held old writing as well as new paintings. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.8.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The Shah Jahan Album held old writing as well as new paintings. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.8.options.1.text.source: An album can give an old work a new setting.
questions.8.options.1.text.back: An album can give an old work a new setting

questions.8.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Like Mir 'Ali Haravi's writing, the old page gets new borders in a new book.
questions.8.options.1.feedback.back: Correct. The old page gets new borders in a new book, like Mir 'Ali Haravi's writing.

questions.8.options.2.text.source: Old writing must stay just as it was made.
questions.8.options.2.text.back: Old writing must always stay as it was

questions.8.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Mughal artists painted new borders around older writing. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.8.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Mughal artists painted new borders around older writing. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.9.question.source: In Akbar's House of Books, how was one painting often made?
questions.9.question.back: In Akbar's House of Books, how was one painting often made?

questions.9.options.0.text.back: Several specialists worked on it together

questions.9.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. One artist might plan it, others add colour, and experts paint faces or animals.
questions.9.options.0.feedback.back: Correct. One artist might plan it, others add colour, and specialists paint faces or animals.

questions.9.options.1.text.source: One artist did every part alone.
questions.9.options.1.text.back: One artist did every part alone

questions.9.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Painters worked with writers, decorators and bookbinders. Several people could work on one picture. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.9.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Painters worked with calligraphers, decorators and bookbinders. Several people could work on one picture. Go back to Lesson 5.

questions.9.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Akbar was a patron. He ordered the work, and skilled makers made it. Look back at Lesson 5.
questions.9.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Akbar was a patron. He ordered the work, and skilled makers made it. Go back to Lesson 5.

results.high.source: Well done. You know a lot about how objects connect to the people who made and used them.
results.high.back: Well done. You know a lot about how objects connect to the people who made and used them.

results.middle.source: Good work. You remember many of the main ideas. Look back at any lesson you want to check.
results.middle.back: Good work. You remember many of the main ideas. Go back to any lesson you want to review.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 1–5, then try again whenever you like.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Go back to Lessons 1–5, then try again whenever you like.
